source_text: [Καὶ τοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ἔθνει ἀσεβοῦς καὶ πλάνου σιμωνιανοῦ διδάγματος κατεφρόνησα.] Ἐὰν δὲ ὑμεῖς τοῦτο προγράψητε, ἡμεῖς τοῖς πᾶσι φανερὸν ποιήσαιμεν, ἵνα εἰ δύναιντο μεταθῶνται· τούτου γε μόνου χάριν τούσδε τοὺς λόγους συνετάξαμεν. Οὐκ ἔστι δὲ ἡμῶν τὰ διδάγματα κατὰ κρίσιν σώφρονα αἰσχρά, ἀλλὰ πάσης μὲν φιλοσοφίας ἀνθρωπείου ὑπέρτερα· εἰ δὲ μή, κἂν σωταδείοις καὶ φιλαινιδείοις καὶ ἀρχεστρατείοις καὶ ἐπικουρείοις καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις τοῖς τοιούτοις ποιητικοῖς διδάγμασιν οὐχ ὅμοια, οἷς ἐντυγχάνειν πᾶσι, καὶ λεγομένοις καὶ γεγραμμένοις, συγκεχώρηται. Καὶ παυσόμεθα λοιπόν, ὅσον ἐφ᾿ ἡμῖν ἦν πράξαντες, καὶ προσεπευξάμενοι τῆς ἀληθείας καταξιωθῆναι τοὺς πάντη πάντας ἀνθρώπους. Εἴη οὖν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀξίως εὐσεβείας καὶ φιλοσοφίας τὰ δίκαια ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῶν κρῖναι.
thought_title: Closing appeal for publication and just judgment
orientation: Justin is concluding his Second Apology to the Roman Senate and people, asking them to publish his defense and to judge rightly.
pass_a_gloss: And I despised the impious and deceitful teaching of the Simonians in my nation. But if you publish this, we would make it clear to all, so that if they are able they may change their mind; for this reason alone we composed these words. Our teachings are not shameful according to sound judgment, but are superior to all human philosophy; if not, at least they are not like the Sotadean and Philainidean and Archestratean and Epicurean and the other such poetic teachings, which all are permitted to encounter, both spoken and written. And we will stop henceforth, having done as much as was in our power, and having prayed that all people everywhere may be deemed worthy of the truth. May it be then that you also judge the just things for yourselves worthily of piety and philosophy.

choices.term: τοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ἔθνει ἀσεβοῦς καὶ πλάνου σιμωνιανοῦ διδάγματος
choices.english: the impious and deceitful teaching of Simon in my nation
choices.why: Keeps the genitive chain literal and preserves the adjective pair modifying the teaching, with Simon's name as the source of the teaching.
rejected: the impious and deceitful Simonian teaching in my nation
the teaching of the impious and deceitful Simonian in my nation

choices.why: The optative with ἵνα expresses purpose; 'make it clear' preserves the causative sense of φανερὸν ποιεῖν.
The middle voice of μετατίθημι here means to change one's own position or opinion, not merely to be moved.

choices.term: σωταδείοις καὶ φιλαινιδείοις καὶ ἀρχεστρατείοις καὶ ἐπικουρείοις
choices.english: Sotadean and Philainidean and Archestratean and Epicurean
choices.why: These are proper adjectives from authors known for obscene or indulgent poetry; transliterating preserves the reference to specific authors.
rejected: obscene and lewd and gluttonous and Epicurean

choices.english: may be deemed worthy of the truth
choices.why: The genitive with καταξιόω is standard; the passive infinitive after προσευξάμενοι expresses the content of the prayer.
rejected: may be counted worthy of the truth

choices.english: judge the just things for yourselves
choices.why: ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῶν means 'on your own behalf' or 'for yourselves'; the phrase asks them to render a just verdict in their own interest.
rejected: judge what is just for yourselves
decide the just things on your own behalf

pass_b_english: I also despised the impious and deceitful teaching of the Simonians in my own nation. If you publish this, we will make it clear to everyone, so that they may change their mind if they can. It was for this reason alone that we composed these words.

Our teachings are not shameful by any sound judgment. They are superior to every human philosophy. Or if they are not, they are at least not like the teachings of Sotades, Philaenis, Archestratus, and Epicurus, and the other such poetic doctrines, which everyone is permitted to encounter, both spoken and written.

And now we will stop, having done as much as was in our power, and having prayed that all people everywhere may be deemed worthy of the truth. May you also judge what is just on your own behalf, in a manner worthy of piety and philosophy.

problems.why: Brief maps 'Σιμωνιανοῦ' to 'Simonian'; 'Simon' alone obscures it's a sect.
problems.ruling: σιμωνιανοῦ means 'Simonian' (adjective/sect name), not 'Simon'; 'Simon' misleads reader about reference.

edits.old: I also despised the impious and deceitful teaching of Simon in my nation.
edits.new: I also despised the impious and deceitful teaching of the Simonians in my nation.

fixed: Changed 'Simon' to 'the Simonians' to reflect the sectarian term σιμωνιανοῦ.

last_rejected.quote: not like the Sotadean, Philainidean, Archestratean, and Epicurean teachings and the other such poetic doctrines
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐχ ὅμοια, οἷς ἐντυγχάνειν πᾶσι, καὶ λεγομένοις καὶ γεγραμμένοις, συγκεχώρηται
last_rejected.why: English omits that everyone is permitted to encounter these; 'which everyone is permitted to encounter' modifies the doctrines, but the Greek says encountering them is permitted to all—this is present but awkward. Actually the 'which' clause is there. Re-reading: 'which everyone is permitted to encounter, both spoken and written'—this is present. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'which everyone is permitted to encounter, both spoken and written'—no omission; rendering is accurate.

last_rejected.why: ποιητικοῖς here likely 'of poets/poetical' in sense of obscene/lascivious poetry, not 'poetic' as artistic; but 'poetic doctrines' is within range. Actually Sotades, Philainis, Archestratus were known for obscene verse. 'Poetic' is accurate but misses connotation; not an error.
last_rejected.ruling: ποιητικοῖς means 'poetic'; connotation of obscene verse is contextually implied but 'poetic doctrines' is within normal range.

last_rejected.source_quote: [Καὶ τοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ἔθνει ἀσεβοῦς καὶ πλάνου σιμωνιανοῦ διδάγματος κατεφρόνησα.]
last_rejected.why: Bracketed text in source indicates editorial uncertainty; but if included in source, English includes it. Actually English has 'I also despised'—this is present. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'I also despised' renders κατεφρόνησα; bracketed source text is translated; no omission.

polish.changed: Clarified the unnamed poetic teachers by converting adjectives to personal names, resolved the Simonians reference as a named group, and broke the long second paragraph into clearer sentences while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: the Sotadean, Philainidean, Archestratean, and Epicurean teachings
notes.why: Three of these four adjectives are unexplained; a modern reader cannot identify Sotadean, Philainidean, or Archestratean teachings.
notes.fix: Note these refer to obscene poetry (Sotades), erotic manuals (Philainis), and gastronomy (Archestratus).

notes.why: Group named without explanation; a modern reader cannot place them.
notes.fix: Identify as followers of Simon Magus, a Gnostic sect.

notes.why: Ambiguous: does Justin mean his birthplace (Flavia Neapolis in Samaria) or the Roman nation addressed?
notes.fix: Clarify: 'among my own people' or 'in my homeland.'
